references.text: Bet-peor is mentioned here in connection with Israel's sin with Moabite women and the idolatry of Baal-peor, which occurred while they were camped in this area.
Peor is the mountain where Balak took Balaam to curse Israel, and it lies in the same geographical region as Bet-peor.
Moses reminds the people of the events at Baal-peor, where those who followed this idol were destroyed by the Lord.
The place is described again as the valley opposite Bet-peor, in the land of Sihon, king of the Amorites.
Moses was buried in a valley in the land of Moab, opposite Bet-peor, the same area mentioned here.
Bet-peor is mentioned as a city given to the tribe of Reuben as part of their inheritance.
Hosea refers to Baal-peor as the place where Israel devoted themselves to shame and became detestable like what they loved.
